lessons.title: Capital Gains Under the Income-tax Act, 2025: What Changed and What Did Not

body.text: The Income-tax Act, 2025 rewrote the rulebook's language and numbering, not the maths of capital gains. The rates, holding periods and exemption limit you pay on today are the same ones that applied before 1 April 2026.

children.text: Rhea, an HR manager in Gurugram, opens a two-year-old blog post on mutual fund tax. It talks about "section 112A", "assessment year 2025-26" and "previous year". Her CA's new checklist talks about "section 198" and "tax year 2026-27". Is this the same tax, or did something change? This lesson gives you the map so you can read old and new material with equal confidence.

The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961 from 1 April 2026. It was designed as a simplification: shorter sections, tables instead of long provisos, and a single "tax year" instead of two overlapping year concepts. The substance of capital gains taxation was carried over almost intact. The separate Finance Act, 2026, passed with Budget 2026, made a couple of real policy changes, which you will see at the end of this lesson.
Change 1: "Tax Year" Replaces Two Confusing Terms

markDefs.definition: Under section 3 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, the twelve-month period from 1 April to 31 March in which income is earned. It replaces the separate "previous year" and "assessment year" concepts of the 1961 Act.

children.text: Under the 1961 Act, income earned in a "previous year" was taxed in the following "assessment year". The 2025 Act uses one term, the
, defined in section 3. The tax year is simply the financial year in which you earn the income.

Which Law Applies to Your Sale?

events.title: Transfers governed by the 1961 Act
events.description: A sale on 25 March 2026 falls in financial year 2025-26. It is assessed in assessment year 2026-27 under the old Act, using old section numbers.

events.title: Old-Act returns are still being filed
events.description: Returns for financial year 2025-26 are filed during 2026 under the 1961 Act, even though the new Act is already in force.

events.title: Transfers governed by the 2025 Act
events.description: A sale on 10 April 2026 falls in tax year 2026-27 and is governed by the new Act and its section numbers.

events.title: First returns under the new Act
events.description: Returns for tax year 2026-27 are filed in 2027 using forms and schedules aligned to the 2025 Act.

body.text: Do not mix the two years. Gains from sales up to 31 March 2026 go in your return for assessment year 2026-27 under the old Act. Gains from sales on or after 1 April 2026 go in your return for tax year 2026-27 under the new Act. There is no gap year and no double filing.

body.title: Old Law or New Law?
body.question: Rhea redeemed equity mutual fund units on 28 March 2026 and sold Nifty BeES units on 6 April 2026. Which statement is correct?
options: Both sales are governed by the Income-tax Act, 2025 because she files both returns after 1 April 2026
The March redemption is governed by the 1961 Act, and the April sale by the 2025 Act
Both sales are governed by the 1961 Act until the first new-Act return is filed in 2027
She can choose which Act applies to each sale
body.explanation: The law that applies follows the date of transfer, not the date of filing. The 28 March 2026 redemption belongs to financial year 2025-26 under the 1961 Act. The 6 April 2026 sale belongs to tax year 2026-27 under the 2025 Act. There is no option to choose.

children.text: Almost every capital gains provision has a new number. Your broker's tax P&L, older blogs and even some CA reports will keep quoting old numbers for a while, so it pays to recognise both.

body.text: You do not need to memorise this table. Learn the three you will see most often as an investor: 111A becomes 196, 112 becomes 197 and 112A becomes 198. The rest you can look up when needed.

body.title: Translate the Old Section
body.textWithBlank: A 2024 blog post says long-term gains on listed shares above ₹1.25 lakh are taxed at 12.5% under section 112A. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the same rule is in section ___.
body.explanation: Section 112A of the 1961 Act corresponds to section 198 of the 2025 Act. The rate of 12.5% and the ₹1.25 lakh exemption carried over unchanged.

cards.definition: Now section 196. STCG on listed equity, equity funds and equity ETFs where STT is paid, at 20%.
Now section 198. LTCG on listed equity above ₹1.25 lakh a year, at 12.5%.
Now section 197. LTCG on other assets such as property, gold and unlisted shares, at 12.5%.
Now section 85. Exemption for reinvesting long-term gains from land or buildings in specified bonds.
Now section 76. Debt funds bought from 1 April 2023, unlisted bonds and MLDs deemed short-term.
Now section 2(101). Defines short-term capital asset and the 12 and 24 month holding periods.

body.label: Budget 2026 on Rates and Holding Periods
body.context: Everything you learned in Lessons 1 to 3 about capital assets, transfers, holding periods and computation applies to tax year 2026-27 exactly as it did to transfers from 23 July 2024 onwards. Only the section numbers moved.

children.text: Two Real Changes From the Finance Act, 2026
While the new Act itself was a rewrite, Budget 2026 made two policy changes that matter to ordinary investors from 1 April 2026.

body.caption: Share buybacks: how tax on an ordinary shareholder changed

cells: Exempt in the shareholder's hands. The company paid buyback tax.
Entire buyback amount taxed as dividend at slab rate. The cost of the shares became a capital loss.
Taxed as capital gains on buyback price minus cost. Promoters pay an additional tax on top.

body.title: Buyback Under the New Rules
body.prompt: In 2026, a Nifty 50 IT company buys back shares at ₹1,900 each. Rhea is not a promoter. She tenders 50 shares that she bought 14 months earlier at ₹1,500 each, and all 50 are accepted. Ignoring expenses, what capital gain arises in rupees?
body.explanation: Buyback proceeds are 50 × ₹1,900 = ₹95,000. Cost is 50 × ₹1,500 = ₹75,000. Capital gain is ₹20,000. Under the rules that applied from 1 October 2024 to 31 March 2026, she would instead have been taxed on the full ₹95,000 as dividend at her slab rate, with ₹75,000 recorded as a capital loss. Prices here are illustrative.

body.title: Two Sovereign Gold Bond Holdings
body.scenario: Rhea holds two Sovereign Gold Bond tranches. She subscribed to Tranche A directly from RBI when it was issued. She bought Tranche B units on NSE from another investor in 2023. She plans to hold both until maturity.
body.prompt: After the Finance Act, 2026 change, which holding can still give a tax-free gain at maturity?
body.modelAnswer: Only Tranche A. From 1 April 2026, the capital gains exemption on redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds at maturity is limited to investors who subscribed at original issue and held continuously until maturity. Tranche B was bought in the secondary market, so its gain at maturity is taxable as a capital gain. Chapter 3 covers how SGB gains are taxed in detail.

body.title: Update Your Tax Vocabulary
steps: Use "tax year" for sales from 1 April 2026 and keep "assessment year" only for older returns
When a broker report, blog or CA note quotes 111A, 112 or 112A, translate it to 196, 197 or 198
Treat anything written before 1 April 2026 as correct on rates, but check the section numbers
Check whether any buyback you took part in happened before or after 1 April 2026
Note which of your Sovereign Gold Bonds were bought at original issue and which on the exchange

points: The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies to transfers from 1 April 2026; earlier transfers stay under the 1961 Act
"Tax year" replaces "previous year" and "assessment year", and simply means the financial year you earn the income
Section numbers changed: 111A is now 196, 112 is now 197 and 112A is now 198
Rates, the ₹1.25 lakh equity exemption, holding periods and the computation method did not change
From 1 April 2026, buybacks are taxed as capital gains for ordinary shareholders again
The tax-free SGB maturity benefit now applies only to original subscribers who hold until maturity

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not tax or investment advice. Section references reflect the Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by the Finance Act, 2026, with corresponding 1961 Act sections alongside. Examples are illustrative. Tax rules change with each Union Budget, so verify current provisions or consult a qualified tax professional before acting.
